question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -2 \\ -3 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

 
The matrix $A$ has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=3.$
Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D={P}^{-1}AP.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/cf6294308a5a05ded00fc272cddd2f1a602ce1f574321f3ebd313f6c53460715.svg) 
The matrix $A$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_1=2,$ $\lambda_2=1,$ and $\lambda_3=0.$
Find a diagonal matrix $D$ and an invertible matrix $P$ such that $D=P^{-1}AP.$
current_example.worked_solution:
We apply the diagonalization algorithm.

**Step 1.**  Notice that we are already given the eigenvalues of the matrix: 

$\qquad$ $\lambda_1=2,\quad$ $\lambda_2=1, \quad$ $\lambda_3=0.$ 

**Step 2.** Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ Applying our usual method, we get the following.

- For $\lambda_1=2,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-2I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-2I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives us the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/ef677b6e2696a9bcd9d27bcb7dcdee30f9e33161a9e3255aad1e4cada6294c82.svg)

- For $\lambda_2=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives us the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/2ab07b57330e01e1936cecb9a835ab8be402ee4af38bde0b1a54b91dfcd943fb.svg)

- For $\lambda_3=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-0I & =A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-0I)\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ gives us the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14153509/assets/71ed0527ac4bba575959e0155f428e1355ce1a74a2053abb7f8093cc819ac245.svg)

**Step 3.** We construct the diagonal matrix $D$ and the invertible matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:
